headline: Is a growing economy becoming more financially fragile?
method: Snapshot of separately timed U.S. macroeconomic and financial indicators. Do not add dollar figures across incompatible financial instruments or interpret stress signals as a probability of a crash.

metrics.label: U.S. output
metrics.interpretation: Economic activity expanded. This does not demonstrate that every household's inflation-adjusted purchasing power rose.

metrics.label: Inflation-adjusted pay
metrics.measure: Real average hourly earnings, all private-sector employees, seasonally adjusted
metrics.interpretation: Average real hourly earnings fell over the year. Not a direct measure of median household income or inequality.

metrics.label: Consumer inflation
metrics.measure: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, 12-month change
metrics.interpretation: Prices rose on average; inflation is not the same as a decline in all real wages or a forecast of future inflation.

metrics.label: Household debt
metrics.measure: Household debt balances; down $13 billion from Q1
metrics.interpretation: The stock of debt alone does not establish that debt service is unaffordable; debt decreased slightly quarter over quarter.

metrics.label: Credit card debt
metrics.measure: Credit card balances; up $21 billion from Q1
metrics.interpretation: Credit card balances rose but credit-card delinquency transition rates remained broadly steady in the report.

financing.period: IMF October 2026 analysis of 14 publicly disclosed AI-related transactions since 2023
financing.interpretation: Distinct financial instruments across the IMF's reviewed sample. Figures are neither realized losses nor independent additive exposures. Financing arrangements may interconnect firm valuations and revenue outlooks.

pathways.title: AI expectations disappoint
pathways.trigger: Company revenues or investment returns fall short of expectations
pathways.transmission: Equity valuations and related credit exposures decline
pathways.householdImpact: Potential job cuts, reduced retirement assets and tighter lending

pathways.title: Borrowing becomes more expensive
pathways.trigger: Bond yields rise on inflation, issuance or fiscal concerns
pathways.transmission: Refinancing pressures on businesses, lenders and governments
pathways.householdImpact: Potential pressure on mortgages, credit costs and public budgets

pathways.title: Consumer credit weakens
pathways.trigger: Income or employment deterioration increases payment distress
pathways.transmission: Lenders tighten standards and household spending slows
pathways.householdImpact: Harder credit access and higher job-loss vulnerability

evidenceRules: No numeric forecast of a 2027 crash is supported by these sources.
No company or individual is accused of causing a crash without case-specific evidence.
Disaggregate household exposure by income, geography and timing where reliable data exists.
Distinguish business ownership, financing, lobbying and direct causal price effects.
No automatic mapping from a ZIP to a person, political affiliation, company exposure or projected loss.

connections.label: Everyday cost categories
connections.scope: Nine issue categories with separate geographically labeled evidence

connections.label: Ownership and price mechanisms
connections.scope: Documented ownership is not proven price causation

connections.label: Political money and business
connections.scope: Candidates for investigation, not proven policy influence

pending.reason: Must refresh debt and delinquency indicators when the New York Fed releases a new vintage
Avoid treating September purchasing-power changes as the latest after the next BLS release
Reconcile legal entities, guarantees, counterparties and public filing dates before drawing company-network edges
No causally established ZIP-specific economic-loss figure; avoid invented household premiums
Confirm each close with a licensed daily series; examine earnings, credit, employment and data-center investment before concluding market losses are spreading to households.

marketStress.scope: US closing-price-index drawdowns from each series' previous record close (different peak dates)
marketStress.headline: AI-related shares have sold off far more sharply than the broad U.S. market
marketStress.summary: The November 5 drop was severe, but the S&P 500 partly rebounded by November 9. A concentrated semiconductor sell-off is not evidence that the whole U.S. economy is in recession.

measures.label: S&P 500
measures.interpretation: Broad large-cap U.S. market. Down 3.44% from its October 6 closing high after the November 9 rebound.

measures.label: Nasdaq Composite
measures.interpretation: Technology-heavy benchmark; its decline is larger than the broad market's.

measures.label: PHLX Semiconductor
measures.interpretation: Semiconductor index; its June peak is not the same starting date as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq peaks.

historicalSample.description: Provider-reported U.S. index record-to-record drawdown episodes since 1928; not a model of future crash probability

pathways.label: Workers and retirement
pathways.text: A longer decline could pressure AI-related hiring, compensation and retirement portfolios; household incidence is not yet established.
pathways.followup: Track verified payrolls, earnings calls and fund exposure.

pathways.label: Financing and credit
pathways.text: Valuation declines could affect equity financing, borrowing capacity and investment plans. No system-wide credit contagion is demonstrated.
pathways.followup: Track credit spreads, financing defaults, capital expenditure and lenders.

pathways.label: Power and local infrastructure
pathways.text: Delayed AI data-center projects could alter anticipated electricity demand, grid investment and local tax plans; these effects differ by region.
pathways.followup: Track confirmed utility filings, project status and rate cases.

safeguards: Price-index drawdowns exclude dividends and do not equal portfolio or household losses.
Each current drawdown starts at its own record date; these are not identical holding-period returns.
The historical chart compares S&P 500 drawdowns only. It is not a projection of the current sell-off.
The 56-event historical sample begins at 6% declines; the latest S&P 500 decline is smaller and should not be assigned a sample-derived crash probability.
A fall in AI-related stocks alone does not establish a recession, criminal conduct or the cause of household price increases.
Data are a dated November 9 snapshot; a live view requires a refreshed, licensed source and validation.
marketStress.sourceType: FRED/S&P index observation; AP reporting; Kadoa provider-derived comparisons; independent semiconductor check
